quarterly_data.quarter: Ebara results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Precision Machinery orders (FY2026 Q2 results presentation, company's Q&A summary): Hosoda said equipment orders rose rapidly in 1Q and moderated somewhat in 2Q, part of 2Q demand having been brought forward into 1Q, but overall order levels remain very strong; component orders have risen for four consecutive quarters, and he expects 2H order levels at least as strong as 1H. Nambu: besides logic customers, where Ebara has traditionally been strong, memory customers also placed very robust orders; equipment orders rose more sharply because customers order earlier to secure production slots; the revised full-year Precision Machinery orders target is JPY 550 billion, driven mainly by higher volumes of existing products, and he is gaining confidence that next year could be very strong. The forecast takes strong Chinese investment and gradually more active NAND investment into account, assuming China demand stays at roughly current levels rather than rising sharply.
quarterly_data.figure: Precision Machinery full-year orders target JPY 550 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Ebara results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Revenue timing and capacity (Q2 results Q&A summary): Nambu said lead times currently range from about six to twelve months, so most equipment orders received in 1H will become revenue next fiscal year; against a WFE market growth assumption of +18%, Ebara plans Precision Machinery revenue growth of +24.2%; the limited JPY 3.5 billion operating-profit uplift reflects a revenue increase weighted to lower-margin components and project mix. On capacity, including the new building completed last year, Ebara has sufficient production capability to meet demand through the current medium-term plan; Hosoda said the Kumamoto plant expansion completed last year gives sufficient capacity for the foreseeable future while additional capex ahead of market growth is continuously evaluated, and that the group is tracking ahead of schedule on revenue against its E-Plan 2028 JPY 1.2 trillion target, though some orders have lead times beyond one year.
quarterly_data.figure: lead times about 6 to 12 months; Precision Machinery revenue growth plan +24.2% vs WFE +18%

quarterly_data.quarter: Ebara results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Energy business (Q2 results Q&A summary): Hosoda said modernization and automation work at the Jeannette plant in the U.S. caused operational loss-related costs of a little over JPY 1 billion in 1H, largely resolved during 1H; Miyaki said the direct causes were basic machining errors and process-management mistakes during large equipment replacement and personnel reallocation, and that the JPY 3 billion downward revision to the full-year operating profit forecast combines the U.S. plant losses and the Middle East situation (Hosoda confirmed roughly JPY 2 billion and JPY 1 billion respectively). The Middle East situation cut 1H by JPY 1.6 billion, mainly ordered products that could not ship because of customer-side logistics, expected to be recognised in 2H; the full-year impact is assumed at negative JPY 1 billion. Fuchida: the yen weakened about JPY 10 against the U.S. dollar year on year, adding about JPY 20 billion to 1H revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Jeannette plant losses a little over JPY 1 billion in 1H; Middle East impact JPY 1.6 billion in 1H, JPY 1 billion full year; FX about JPY 20 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Ebara results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New product (Q2 results Q&A summary): Ebara launched a chiller able to operate at minus 60 degrees Celsius for ultra-low-temperature applications such as cryogenic etching - a new market entry using its thermal-management and pump technologies; Nagata said etching has typically run at around minus 30 degrees Celsius, that this range is a relatively new frontier where many competitors are still developing products, and that its main differentiator is power consumption 30% to 50% lower than conventional competing products (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: minus 60 degrees Celsius; power consumption 30% to 50% lower
